notes: ab reported 'Failed requests' due to Length mismatches (499/500 on /bicycles, 275/500 on /bicycles/1); this reflects per-request variation in dynamic HTML byte length (e.g. CSRF tokens), not real HTTP errors -- both endpoints returned 200 consistently via curl checks and ab's own timing/throughput figures are unaffected.

Ruby 4.0 removed 'benchmark' from the default gem set (it's now an optional gem requiring a Gemfile entry). Since gem/app changes were disallowed, require 'benchmark' raised LoadError under this app's Bundler context. Substituted Process.clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) (Ruby core, not a gem) for wall-clock timing in the microbenchmarks -- functionally equivalent to Benchmark.realtime, which itself wraps clock_gettime.

Port 3000 was occupied by the sibling A/B comparison app (r3, Ruby 3.3.12) during this run, confirming both apps were being benchmarked concurrently as expected; the HTTP load test used port 3100 instead with no conflict.
